scope: Corollary 4.2 (Interlacing with endpoint abutments) of the manuscript “Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one” (preprints/Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bf15a86507a10184), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G be a finite ordinary graph embedded in a closed disk, with the edge odds of this section. Let the nonempty electrodes A, C, B, D be carried, in that cyclic order, by four accessible nondegenerate closed boundary arcs. Their relative interiors are pairwise disjoint, and only consecutive arcs in this cyclic order may share an endpoint. Assume A ∩ C = A ∩ B = C ∩ D = ∅. At every shared boundary incidence, the full physical-edge fan lies on the disk side. In a slightly enlarged disk, choose distinct boundary points s, s′, exterior spokes from A to s and from B to s′, and outward access arcs from every C vertex to one of the two open components of the enlarged boundary minus {s, s′} and from every D vertex to the other. The spokes and access arcs can be chosen with interiors disjoint from the graph and from one another. They may meet only at a designated shared electrode endpoint, except that the A spokes may meet at s and the B spokes at s′. Then (4.2) holds.
